Product brief

Pipeup

Pipe up, right where the work is.

Product skillWrite or update the brief, asking for every missing fact; regenerate and review the documents; build the shared folder.

Problem

People share work as standalone HTML files: reports, specs, prototypes and slide decks, many of them written by AI agents. Those files have no good way to collect feedback. Reviewers reply in chat threads that lose the context of what they were looking at, and the author (or the agent working for them) has to guess where each remark belongs.

Audience

  • MLMaya Lindqvistsomeone sent them an HTML file; they want to say what they think about a sentence, a block or a spot, and hand it back, with no account to make.
  • TATom Adeyemithey made the page (or an agent did), add one line to it, and want every comment pinned to the exact place so an agent can act on it.

Value

Pipeup turns any HTML page into a reviewable document with one script tag. Reviewers select words, click a block or drop a pin and comment in place. Comments stay in their own browser, and Copy comments as Markdown turns them into text that says exactly where each comment is, ready to send to the author or paste into an AI agent.

What sets it apart

  • No accounts and no servers: Pipeup itself never sends anything anywhere, and a page opened from disk works.
  • The page stays the author's: nothing is restyled, moved or covered, and outside comment mode the page behaves exactly as before.
  • Comments carry their place: the slide or section, the element, the quoted words or the pin, so an agent knows where to act.
  • One set of gestures covers text, blocks, pins and the page as a whole.

Not for

  • Reviewing images or PDFs on their own.
  • A hosted service, accounts, dashboards or notifications: sharing and live review are optional add-ons the author chooses.
  • Rich comments: formatting, images or embedded content. Comments are plain text with line breaks and links.
  • Replacing the chat or tracker where decisions are made; Pipeup collects the feedback and hands it on.

Platform

  • Runs on: current desktop and mobile browsers, on any HTML page opened from disk, served locally or hosted on the web.
  • Appearance: the light theme by default; the person can switch to dark or automatic from the comment control's menu, and the choice is remembered for that page in that browser.
  • Sizes: phones from 390 px wide upward; on wide windows the comment column sits beside the content, and on narrow screens threads open below what they are about and All comments takes the full width.
  • Input: pointer, keyboard (Shift+Alt+C, ⇧⌥C on a Mac, toggles comment mode; Esc steps out) and touch.
  • Start and stop: the page opens with its comments showing and comment mode off; comments, the person's name and the hidden choice are kept in that browser for that page.

Success criteria

SC-001
A reviewer with no account comments on a sentence within a minute of opening the page. Measure: Open question How will this be observed: moderated sessions, or something counted?
SC-002
An author pastes copied comments into a coding agent and the agent finds every place without asking. Measure: Open question How many pastes, and who judges that the agent found the place?
